attrs.management_says: Gross margin improved 80 bps due to sales mix (60 bps) and lower input costs (50 bps), with DTC growth reducing outlet excess-inventory sales.
attrs.numbers_show: Gross margin rose 47.9%→48.7% (E35, E36, E37). The mix shift toward DTC (higher margin) aligns with the margin improvement and could support faster cash collection. However, the magnitude of wholesale growth (unquantified) and the CFO collapse suggest the mix shift was insufficient to offset cash-flow pressures elsewhere.
attrs.verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.management_says: Gross margin improved 80 bps driven by sales mix (60 bps) and lower input costs (50 bps).
attrs.numbers_show: Gross margin rose from 47.9% to 48.7% (E35). This profitability improvement supports higher net income but does not directly explain receivables or cash flow movements; it is consistent with the overall narrative.

attrs.management_says: Gross margin improved 80 bps due to sales mix (60 bps: less excess inventory through factory house outlets, lower wholesale footwear proportion) and lower North American apparel/accessories input costs (50 bps).
attrs.numbers_show: Gross margin rose from 47.9% to 48.7%. The receivables DSO improvement and slower receivables growth support a mix shift away from lower-margin wholesale/outlet sales toward higher-margin direct-to-consumer.

attrs.reason: Gross margin improved 80 bps (E35). The MD&A attributes this to a ~60 bps sales mix benefit from reduced outlet excess-inventory sales and lower wholesale footwear proportion (E36), and a ~50 bps benefit from lower input costs (E37). The DTC revenue growth of $176.8M (E34) is visible in the numbers and supports a mix shift toward higher-margin channels. The aggregate COGS growth (25.1%) lagging revenue growth (27.1%) is consistent with lower input costs or favorable mix. While the input cost benefit is not directly isolated, the overall margin expansion is consistent with the cited drivers at the stated scale.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 80 bps gross margin improvement (47.9%→48.7%, E35) is corroborated by the 33.2% DTC revenue growth ($176.8M, E34) shifting mix toward higher-margin channels (E36) and management's stated 50 bps input cost benefit (E37). The DTC mix shift is visible in the numbers at a scale consistent with the claimed 60 bps mix benefit, and the margin expansion supports faster cash conversion from DTC sales.

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.reason: Gross margin improved 80 bps (47.9% to 48.7%) per MD&A and computed from revenue/COGS (E1, E2, E13, E14, E35). However, the causal drivers—60 bps from sales mix shift and 50 bps from lower input costs—are not independently visible in the numbers. Segment data is geographic (E55), not by channel (DTC vs wholesale), and input costs are not disclosed. The explanation rests on management's word.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: Gross margin improved 80 bps due to a favorable sales mix shift toward higher-margin DTC channels and lower apparel input costs, as reported by management.

attrs.reason: Gross margin improved 80 bps, but the named drivers (sales mix shift away from excess inventory/wholesale footwear, and lower input costs) are not directly visible in the reported numbers. The MD&A attributes 60 bps to sales mix and 50 bps to input costs, but the evidence pack lacks channel-level gross margins or input cost data to corroborate the magnitude. Receivables DSO improvement is consistent with a channel shift but does not quantify the gross margin impact.
